ukberi-tibyan:101-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنَى أُولَئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ (١٠١) لَا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَهَا وَهُمْ فِي مَا اشْتَهَتْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ خَالِدُونَ (١٠٢) لَا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الْفَزَعُ الْأَكْبَرُ وَتَتَلَقَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ هَذَا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ (١٠٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنَّا): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «سَبَقَتْ», and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْحُسْنَى».
(لَا يَسْمَعُونَ): it may be a badal (substitute) from «مُبْعَدُونَ», it may be a second khabar (predicate), and it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُبْعَدُونَ».
(هَذَا يَوْمُكُمُ): i.e. saying (يَقُولُونَ).

ukberi-tibyan:104-104.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّمَاءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ كَمَا بَدَأْنَا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ وَعْدًا عَلَيْنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ (١٠٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَوْمَ نَطْوِي): it may be a badal (substitute) from the omitted returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) in His saying «تُوعَدُونَ»; or by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"); or an adverb (ẓarf) for «لَا يَحْزُنُهُمُ»; or by implying اذْكُرْ ("mention").
نَطْوِي is read with nūn, as the plural of majesty; with yāʾ, as the third person; and with tāʾ, leaving the agent unnamed [Translator's note: i.e. تُطْوَى].
(السَّمَاءَ) is (then) in the nominative. The implied form is "a folding like the folding of…" (طَيًّا كَطَيِّ), and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in construct with its object, if we say that السِّجِلّ is the sheet of writing (الْقِرْطَاس).
It is also said: it is the name of an angel or of a scribe, in which case it is put in construct with its agent.
It is also read with kasra on the sīn and the jīm and a doubled lām (السِّجِلِّ).
It is also read likewise except with the lām undoubled.
It is also read with fatḥa on the sīn, the jīm quiescent and the lām undoubled; and with ḍamma on the sīn and the jīm, undoubled and doubled; these are dialectal forms of it.
The lām in «لِلْكِتَابِ» is redundant (zāʾida). [Translator's note: the source writes «لِلْكِتَابِ» (singular) here, while the verse as quoted above reads لِلْكُتُبِ; the singular is a known variant reading.] It is also said: it has the meaning of عَلَى. It is also said: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to طَيّ. And Allah knows best.
His saying, the Exalted: (كَمَا بَدَأْنَا): the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar; i.e. "We shall repeat it with a repetition like its beginning". Concerning the accusative of «أَوَّلَ» there are two views: first, it is accusative governed by بَدَأْنَا; i.e. "We created the first creation". Second, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in نُعِيدُهُ, the meaning being: like the first of its creation.
(وَعْدًا): a maṣdar; i.e. "We promised that with a promise".

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِي الزَّبُورِ مِنْ بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ أَنَّ الْأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِيَ الصَّالِحُونَ (١٠٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنْ بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to كَتَبْنَا, and it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for الزَّبُور, because الزَّبُور has the meaning of الْمَزْبُور, i.e. what is written.

ukberi-tibyan:107-107.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ (١٠٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً): it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "possessing mercy", as Allah the Exalted said: (وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا); and it may have the meaning of رَاحِم ("merciful").

ukberi-tibyan:108-108.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنَّمَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ (١٠٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يُوحَى إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَا): «أَنَّ» is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and the restraining «مَا» (al-kāffa) does not prevent that; the implied form is: "the oneness of my God is revealed to me".
(فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ): هَلْ here is in the form of a question, while the meaning is incitement; i.e. "so will you then submit after this?" — so it refers to the future.

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُلْ آذَنْتُكُمْ عَلَى سَوَاءٍ وَإِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ أَمْ بَعِيدٌ مَا تُوعَدُونَ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْتُمُونَ (١١٠))
His saying, the Exalted: (عَلَى سَوَاءٍ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from both the object and the agent; i.e. being equal in knowledge of what I have informed you of.
(وَإِنْ أَدْرِي): with the yāʾ quiescent, which is the original form; its having fatḥa has been reported as an anomalous (shādhdh) reading. Abū al-Fatḥ [Translator's note: Ibn Jinnī] said: it is a mistake, because «إِنْ» has the meaning of مَا.
Someone else said: the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the yāʾ, so it took a vowel and the hamza remained quiescent; then it was changed into an alif because of the fatḥa before it; then it was changed back into a voweled hamza, because it is treated as something begun with, and beginning with a quiescent letter is impossible.
(أَقَرِيبٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (مَا تُوعَدُونَ) is its fāʿil (agent), because it is supported by the hamza (of interrogation). According to the view of the Basrans it may be construed as being made nominative by بَعِيد, because it is nearer to it.
(مِنَ الْقَوْلِ): a ḥāl from الْجَهْر; i.e. what is spoken openly of speech.

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ رَبِّ احْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَرَبُّنَا الرَّحْمَنُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَى مَا تَصِفُونَ (١١٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (قَالَ رَبِّ): it is read in the form of the imperative [Translator's note: i.e. قُلْ رَبِّ], and in the form of the past. And «احْكُمْ» is as an imperative.
It is also read: رَبِّي احْكُمْ, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
(تَصِفُونَ): with tāʾ and with yāʾ, and it is clear. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَكَذَلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٨٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (نُنْجِي): the majority read it with the two nūns together and the jīm without shadda. It is also read with a single nūn and a doubled jīm (نُجِّي), and there are three views on it:
The first: that it is a past verb, and the yāʾ was made quiescent preferring lightness, and what stands in the place of the fāʿil (agent) is the maṣdar (verbal noun); i.e. "the saving was saved" (نَجَّى النَّجَاءُ). This is weak in two respects: first, making the end of a past verb quiescent; second, putting the maṣdar in the place of the fāʿil while a proper object is present. The second view: that it is an imperfect (future) verb from which the second nūn was changed into a jīm and assimilated; this too is weak.
The third: that its original form is نُنَجِّي, with fatḥa on the second nūn, but it was dropped just as the second tāʾ was dropped in (تَظَاهَرُونَ). This too is weak, for two reasons: first, the second nūn is a radical, namely the first radical (fāʾ) of the word, so dropping it is very far-fetched. Second, its vowel differs from the vowel of the first nūn, so combining the two is not felt to be heavy, unlike «تُظَاهِرُونَ»; do you not see that if you said تُتَحَامَى الْمَظَالِمُ ("injustices are avoided"), dropping the second tāʾ would not be permissible?

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ يَحْيَى وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا وَكَانُوا لَنَا خَاشِعِينَ (٩٠))
His saying, the Exalted: (رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); or a maṣdar according to the meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ رُوحِنَا وَجَعَلْنَاهَا وَابْنَهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ (٩١))
His saying, the Exalted: (وَالَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ): i.e. "and mention the one who…" (وَاذْكُرِ الَّتِي).
It may also be in the position of the nominative; i.e. "and among what is recited to you is the account of the one who…" (وَفِيمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكَ خَبَرُ الَّتِي).
(فِيهَا): refers back to Maryam.
(آيَةً): a second object. Concerning its being singular there are two views:
The first: that Maryam and her son, peace be upon them both, together are a single sign, because the wonder was completed by the two of them. The second: that its implied form is "and We made her a sign, and her son likewise", so آيَةً is the object of the one conjoined to (al-maʿṭūf ʿalayhi). It is also said: what is omitted is the first one, and the آيَةً that is mentioned belongs to the son.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُونِ (٩٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أُمَّتُكُمْ) in the nominative: as the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ; and in the accusative as a badal (substitute) or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).
(أُمَّةً) in the accusative: a ḥāl (circumstantial); and in the nominative, a badal from «أُمَّتُكُمْ», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:93-94.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَاجِعُونَ (٩٣) فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِ وَإِنَّا لَهُ كَاتِبُونَ (٩٤))
His saying, the Exalted: (وَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ): i.e. in their affair (فِي أَمْرِهِمْ); i.e. they split apart. It is also said: تَقَطَّعُوا was made transitive by itself, because it has the meaning of قَطَّعُوا, i.e. they divided. It is also said: it is a tamyīz (specification); i.e. their affair was cut apart (تَقَطَّعَ أَمْرُهُمْ).
(لَهُ): i.e. for the striving (السَّعْي). It is also said: it refers back to مَنْ.

ukberi-tibyan:95-96.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَحَرَامٌ عَلَى قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ (٩٥) حَتَّى إِذَا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُونَ (٩٦).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَحَرَامٌ): it is read with the alif; with kasra on the ḥāʾ and the rāʾ quiescent without an alif (حِرْمٌ); and with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ without an alif (حَرِمٌ). In all of these it is nominative by being a mubtadaʾ (subject); and concerning the khabar (predicate) there are two views:
The first: it is «أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ», and «لَا» is redundant (zāʾida); i.e. their return to the world is impossible. It is also said: it is not redundant; i.e. their not returning from their disobedience is impossible.
The better view is that «أَنَّهُمْ» is a fāʿil (agent) that fills the place of the khabar.
The second: the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "their repentance", or "the hope of their being raised", if you make «لَا» redundant.
It is also said: «حَرَامٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; i.e. "that righteous deed which we mentioned is forbidden". حَرَامٌ and حِرْمٌ are two dialectal forms, like حَلَالٌ and حِلٌّ. Whoever reads with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ makes it an active participle of حَرِمَ, i.e. "it became impossible", like فَلِقَ; and from it is:
يَقُولُ لَا غَائِبٌ مَالِي وَلَا حَرِمٌ
(He says: my wealth is neither absent nor withheld.)
i.e. withheld (مُمْتَنَعٌ).
It is also read «حَرُمَ» as a verb, with kasra on the rāʾ and with ḍamma. (أَنَّهُمْ) is read with fatḥa, as maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and with kasra, as a resumption.
(حَتَّى): attached (mutaʿalliq) in meaning to حَرَامٌ; i.e. the impossibility continues until this time; and it has no governing effect on «إِذَا».
It is also read «مِنْ كُلِّ جَدَثٍ» with jīm and thāʾ, and it has the meaning of الْحَدَب.
(يَنْسِلُونَ) with kasra on the sīn and with ḍamma: two dialectal forms. The apodosis (jawāb) of إِذَا is «فَإِذَا هِيَ». It is also said: its apodosis is قَالُوا يَا وَيْلَنَا; and it is also said: وَاقْتَرَبَ, the wāw being redundant.

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاقْتَرَبَ الْوَعْدُ الْحَقُّ فَإِذَا هِيَ شَاخِصَةٌ أَبْصَارُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَا وَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هَذَا بَلْ كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ (٩٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَإِذَا هِيَ): «إِذَا» is of surprise (mufājaʾa), and it is (an adverb of) place, and what governs it is «شَاخِصَةٌ»; and هِيَ is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa).
(أَبْصَارُ الَّذِينَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «شَاخِصَةٌ» is its khabar (predicate).
(يَاوَيْلَنَا): in the position of the accusative, governed by an implied قَالُوا ("they said").
It may also be that the implied form is يَقُولُونَ ("saying"), so that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنْتُمْ لَهَا وَارِدُونَ (٩٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ): it is read with fatḥa on the ṣād, meaning that with which it is kindled; and with the ṣād quiescent, which is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of حَصَبْتُهَا, "I kindled it"; so it has the meaning of the passive participle (الْمَحْصُوب, "what is kindled").
It is also read with ḍād, with a vowel and quiescent, and with ṭāʾ; and these two have the same meaning.
(أَنْتُمْ لَهَا): it may be a badal (substitute) from «حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ», it may be resumptive, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَهَنَّمَ».

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُعْرِضُونَ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ): هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «مُعْرِضُونَ» is the khabar (predicate). «فِي غَفْلَةٍ» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in معرضون, i.e. "they turned away heedless". It may also be a second khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:2-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ (٢) لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا هَلْ هَذَا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ أَفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُحْدَثٍ): construed on the wording of «ذِكْرٍ» [hence genitive]; had it been put in the nominative according to the position of «مِنْ ذِكْرٍ», it would have been permissible.
And (مِنْ ذِكْرٍ): it may be attached to يأتيهم, or be an adjective of ذكر, or be attached to محدث, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in محدث.
«[Translator's note: the heading here repeats «مِنْ ذِكْرٍ», but the options listed (adjective of ذكر, attached to محدث) fit «مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ», which is evidently what is meant.]»
His saying, Exalted is He: {لاهية}: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَلْعَبُونَ»; it may also be a ḥāl from the wāw in «اسْتَمَعُوهُ».
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا): concerning its position there are three views. The first: the nominative, and in this there are four views. One of them: that it is a badal (substitute) from the wāw in «أَسَرُّوا». The second: that it is the fāʿil (agent), the wāw being a particle marking the plural, not a noun. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being «هَلْ هَذَا», the implied form being: "they say: is this…". The fourth: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who did wrong".
The second view: that it is accusative by an implied أعني ("I mean"). The third: that it is genitive as an adjective of الناس (ayah 1).

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَالَ رَبِّي): it is read (قُلْ) as a command, and (قَالَ) as a report.
(فِي السَّمَاءِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from القول, or a ḥāl from the agent in «يَعْلَمُ», though there is weakness in this; it may also be attached to يعلم.

ukberi-tibyan:5-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (بَلْ قَالُوا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ بَلِ افْتَرَاهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِآيَةٍ كَمَا أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ (٥) مَا آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ (٦) وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ فَاسْأَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ): i.e. "this is jumbled [dreams]".
(كَمَا أُرْسِلَ): i.e. "a bringing [of a sign] like the sending of the former ones".
And (أَهْلَكْنَاهَا): an adjective of قرية, either according to its wording or according to its position.
And (يُوحَى) with yāʾ, with «إِلَيْهِمْ» standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). And (نُوحِي) with nūn, the object being omitted, i.e. "the command and the prohibition".

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَدًا لَا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا خَالِدِينَ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَسَدًا): it is a singular in the place of a plural, and the muḍāf is omitted, i.e. "possessors of bodies". And «لَا يَأْكُلُونَ» is an adjective of أجساد ("bodies").
And (جَعَلْنَاهُمْ): it may be transitive to two objects, or transitive to one, in which case «جَسَدًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) and «لَا يَأْكُلُونَ» another ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:10-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَابًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (١٠) وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً وَأَنْشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا آخَرِينَ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ): the clause is an adjective of كتاب.
And (ذِكْرُكُمْ) is annexed to its object, i.e. "Our mentioning of you".
It may also be annexed to its agent, i.e. "what you mentioned of associating partners [with Allah] and denying the Prophet ﷺ"; the object is then omitted.
And (كَمْ): in the position of the accusative by قصمنا.
And (كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً): an adjective of قرية.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوا بَأْسَنَا إِذَا هُمْ مِنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا هُمْ): [إذا] of surprise (mufājaʾa); «هُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and يركضون the khabar (predicate), and إذا is an adverb for the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:15-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَمَا زَالَتْ تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمْ حَتَّى جَعَلْنَاهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَامِدِينَ (١٥) وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ (١٦) لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا إِنْ كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ (١٧) بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمْ): «تِلْكَ» is in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of زالت, and «دَعْوَاهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate); the reverse is also permissible. The دعوى ("cry") is their saying: «يَا وَيْلَنَا».
And (حَصِيدًا): a second object; the implied form is: "like a harvested crop", and that is why it is not made plural, just as the implied «مِثْل» is not made plural.
And (خَامِدِينَ): it is like هَذَا حُلْوٌ حَامِضٌ ("this is sweet-sour") [i.e. the two together form one predicate]; it may also be an adjective of حصيد.
And (لَاعِبِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in خلقنا.
And (إِنْ كُنَّا): in the sense of "We were not". It is also said: it is conditional.
(فَيَدْمَغُهُ): it was read anomalously in the accusative [فَيَدْمَغَهُ], and this is far-fetched; it is construed according to the meaning, i.e. "with the truth, and then the crushing".
(مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ): a ḥāl, i.e. "and woe be to you, befalling [you]".
And «مَا»: in the sense of الذي, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, or maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ): there are two views on it. One of them: that «مَنْ» is conjoined to the first «مَنْ», the first being a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لَهُ» the khabar (predicate); or it is nominative by the adverbial phrase. On this view «لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the first «مَنْ», or from the second according to the view of those who make it nominative by the adverbial phrase, or from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase that is the khabar, or from the pronoun in عنده. The second view: that the second «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, and «لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ» the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُسَبِّحُونَ): it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun before it.
And (لَا يَفْتُرُونَ): a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in «يُسَبِّحُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنْشِرُونَ (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْأَرْضِ): it is an adjective of آلهة; or attached to اتخذوا, in the sense of the beginning of the extent of the taking.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا اللَّهُ): the nominative is on the basis that «إِلَّا» is an adjective in the sense of غَيْر ("other than"). It cannot be a badal (substitute), because the meaning would then amount to your saying: "If Allah were in them both, they would have been ruined". Do you not see that if you said: مَا جَاءَنِي قَوْمُكَ إِلَّا زَيْدٌ as a badal, the meaning would be: "Zayd alone came to me"?
It is also said: the badal is impossible because what precedes it is affirmative. Nor is the accusative as an exception permissible, for two reasons. One of them: that it is corrupt in meaning. That is because if you say: "If the people had come to me except Zayd, I would have killed them", its meaning is that the killing [was prevented] because Zayd was with the people. So if you put it in the accusative in the ayah, the meaning would be that the ruin of the heavens and the earth was prevented by the presence of Allah the Exalted with the gods, and that involves affirming a god alongside Allah.
If you put it in the nominative as an adjective, nothing like that follows, because the meaning is: "If there were in them both [gods] other than Allah, they would have been ruined".
The second reason: that آلهة here is indefinite, and an indefinite plural is not excepted from, according to a group of the verifying scholars, because it has no generality such that the excepted item would be included in it were it not for the exception.
«[Translator's note: in the example, the text says «كَانَ مَعْنَاهُ أَنَّ الْقَتْلَ لِكَوْنِ زَيْدٍ مَعَ الْقَوْمِ» ("its meaning is that the killing is because Zayd is with the people"); the sense required by the argument is that the killing was prevented because Zayd was among them. The bracketed "[was prevented]" is added for clarity.]»

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ هَذَا ذِكْرُ مَنْ مَعِيَ وَذِكْرُ مَنْ قَبْلِي بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْحَقَّ فَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذِكْرُ مَنْ مَعِيَ): the majority read it with annexation (iḍāfa).
It was also read with tanwīn [ذِكْرٌ مَنْ], on the basis that «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative by the maṣdar (verbal noun).
It may also be in the position of the nominative, the maṣdar being treated as passive (with the agent unnamed).
It is also read likewise, except with kasra on the mīm [ذِكْرٌ مِنْ مَعِيَ]; the implied form is: "this is a reminder from a book with me, and from a book before me", and the like; the qualified noun was omitted.
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْحَقَّ): the majority read it in the accusative by the verb before it.
It was also read in the nominative, on the implied form of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:26-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ (٢٦) لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ وَهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ (٢٧))
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلْ عِبَادٌ): i.e. "rather they are servants".
(مُكْرَمُونَ): light and with the shadda [مُكَرَّمُونَ].
And (يَسْبِقُونَهُ): an adjective in the position of the nominative.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّي إِلَهٌ مِنْ دُونِهِ فَذَلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَذَلِكَ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
It is also said: in the position of the accusative by a verb indicated by «نَجْزِيهِ»; and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
And (كَذَلِكَ): in the position of the accusative by «نَجْزِي», i.e. "a recompense like that".

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوَلَمْ): it is read with the wāw and without it; its parallel has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara at His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ).
(كَانَتَا): the pronoun refers back to the two genera [heavens and earth].
And (رَتْقًا): with sukūn on the tāʾ, i.e. "possessed of closure", or "closed up", like الخَلْق in the sense of المخلوق ("the created").
It is also read with fatḥa on it [رَتَقًا], in the sense of "the closed-up thing", like القَبَض and النَّقَض.
(وَجَعَلْنَا): i.e. "and We created"; the object is «كُلَّ شَيْءٍ», «حَيٍّ» is an adjective, and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent.
It [مِنَ الْمَاءِ] may also be an adjective of كلّ that has been placed before it and so become a ḥāl (circumstantial). It may also be that جعل is in the sense of "made into"; then «مِنَ الْمَاءِ» is the second object.
«حَيًّا» is also read [in the accusative], on the basis that it is an adjective of «كُلَّ», or the second object.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَمِيدَ): i.e. "for fear that it should sway", or "so that it would not sway".
And (فِجَاجًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سُبُلًا». It is also said: سبلًا is a badal (substitute), i.e. "roads, broad ways (سُبُلًا فِجَاجًا)", as has come in the other ayah.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُلٌّ): i.e. "each one of the two" or "of them", and it refers back to the night, the day, the sun and the moon.
And (يَسْبَحُونَ): the khabar (predicate) of «كُلٌّ» according to the meaning, because when each one of them swims, all of them swim.
It is also said: on this view «يَسْبَحُونَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the khabar is «فِي فَلَكٍ».
It is also said: the implied form is "all of them", and the khabar is «يَسْبَحُونَ»; He brought the plural pronoun according to the meaning of «كُلٌّ», and made it masculine like the pronoun of rational beings, because He described them with swimming, which is among the attributes of rational beings.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ): this has been mentioned at His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ (٣٥))
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِتْنَةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); or in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "testing [you]"; or as a maṣdar [mafʿūl muṭlaq] in the sense of نبلوكم, i.e. "We try you with them both with a trial".

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ هُمْ كَافِرُونَ (٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا هُزُوًا): i.e. "an object of mockery", and it is a second object. He repeated the mention of them [هُمْ] for emphasis (tawkīd).

ukberi-tibyan:37-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ (٣٧) وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٣٨) لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ (٣٩) بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ (٤٠))
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ عَجَلٍ): in the position of the accusative by خُلِقَ, figuratively, just as you say: "he was created from clay".
It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "hasty". The apodosis (jawāb) of «لَوْ» is omitted. And «حِينَ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverb. And «بَغْتَةً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ): i.e. "from the command of the Most Merciful"; so it is in the position of the accusative by يكلؤكم. Its parallel is: (يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ).
«[Translator's note: the ayah number is printed as (٤١) in the source; this ayah is 42.]»

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ (٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ): it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ وَآبَاءَهُمْ حَتَّى طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا): this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Raʿd.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا يَسْمَعُ): there are several readings of it whose explanations are clear.
And (إِذَا): accusative by يسمع, or by الدعاء; on this latter view the maṣdar (verbal noun) made definite by alif and lām governs by itself.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَا وَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ (٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ عَذَابِ): an adjective of «نَفْحَةٌ», or in the position of the accusative by مستهم.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ (٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْقِسْطَ): it is singular although it is an adjective of a plural only because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as an adjective.
If you wish, you may say: the implied form is "possessors of justice".
(لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ): i.e. "for its sake". It is also said: it is in the sense of في ("on").
And (شَيْئًا): in the sense of the maṣdar.
And (مِثْقَالَ): in the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان, i.e. "even if the wrong, or the deed, be [the weight…]".
It is also read in the nominative, on the basis that «كَانَ» is complete (tāmma, i.e. "exist").
And (مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ): an adjective of حبة, or of «مِثْقَالَ».
And (أَتَيْنَا): with the short vowel, [meaning] "We brought". It is also read [آتَيْنَا, with the long vowel] in the sense of "We recompensed for it"; so it comes close to the meaning of "We gave", because recompense is a giving. It is not transferred from أتينا, because that has not been transmitted from them [the Arabs].

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَاءً وَذِكْرًا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ (٤٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَضِيَاءً): it is said: the wāw comes in on the adjective, as you say: مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ الْكَرِيمِ وَالْعَالِمِ ("I passed by Zayd, the generous and the learned"); on this view it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "the Criterion, illuminating". It is also said: it is a conjunction, i.e. "We gave him three things: the Criterion, the light and the reminder".

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ (٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective, or the accusative by an implied أعني ("I mean"),
or the nominative by an implied «هُمْ» ("they are"). And «بِالْغَيْبِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا هَذِهِ التَّمَاثِيلُ الَّتِي أَنْتُمْ لَهَا عَاكِفُونَ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ): «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for عالمين (ayah 51), or for رشده, or for آتينا…
It may also be a badal (substitute) from the position of «مِنْ قَبْلُ».
It may also be accusative by an implied أعني ("I mean"), or by an implied اذكر ("remember").
(لَهَا عَاكِفُونَ): it is said: the lām is in the sense of على ("upon"), as in His saying: (لَنْ نَبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفِينَ). It is also said: it keeps its basic meaning, since the meaning is "you are worshippers of them". It is also said: it conveys the sense of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ).

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ (٥٦))
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ): it cannot be attached to «الشاهدين», because of what that would entail of placing [part of] the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative [al-]; so it is for clarification (tabyīn). This has been mentioned in several places.

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَاذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جُذَاذًا): it is read with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra, and these are dialectal variants. It is also said: the ḍamma is on the basis that its singular is جُذَاذَة; the kasra on the basis that its singular is جِذَاذَة with kasra; and the fatḥa as a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الحَصَاد; the implied form is "possessed of fragmentation".
It is also read with ḍamma on the jīm without alif [جُذَذًا], its singular being جُذَّة, like قُبَّة and قُبَب.
It is also read likewise, except with ḍamma on the first dhāl [جُذُذًا], its singular being جَذِيذ, like قَلِيب and قُلُب.
«[Translator's note: the text prints the plural example as «قَلْبٍ»; the pattern being illustrated is قُلُب.]»

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا مَنْ فَعَلَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ (٥٩))
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ فَعَلَ هَذَا): «مَنْ» may be interrogative; then «إِنَّهُ» is a new beginning (istiʾnāf).
It may also be in the sense of الذي; then «إِنَّهُ» and what follows it is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ (٦٠))
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَذْكُرُهُمْ): the second object of سمعنا; and that [second object] can only be something heard, as in your saying: سَمِعْتُ زَيْدًا يَقُولُ كَذَا ("I heard Zayd saying such-and-such"), the meaning being: "I heard Zayd's words".
And (يُقَالُ): an adjective; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial). Concerning the nominative of «إِبْرَاهِيمُ», upon him be peace, there are three views:
One of them: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he is", or "this is". It is also said: a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, i.e. "Ibrāhīm is the doer of that", and the clause is quoted (maḥkiyya). The second: it is a singular vocative (munādā mufrad), so its ḍamma is indeclinable (mabnī). The third: it is the object of (يُقَالُ) [as deputy agent], because the meaning is "Ibrāhīm is mentioned in naming him", so what is meant is the name, not the one named.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا فَأْتُوا بِهِ عَلَى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in their sight", i.e. "plainly visible to them".

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَذَا فَاسْأَلُوهُمْ إِنْ كَانُوا يَنْطِقُونَ (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلْ فَعَلَهُ): the fāʿil (agent) is «كَبِيرُهُمْ».
(هَذَا): an adjective, or a badal (substitute). It is also said: the pause is on «فَعَلَهُ», and the agent is omitted, i.e. "whoever did it did it"; this is far-fetched, because omitting the agent is not admissible.

ukberi-tibyan:65-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا عَلَى رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ (٦٥) قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُكُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى رُءُوسِهِمْ): attached to نكسوا. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and so attached to something omitted.
(مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ): the clause takes the place of the two objects of «عَلِمْتَ», as in His saying: (وَظَنُّوا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ).
And (شَيْئًا): in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "any benefit".
(أُفٍّ لَكُمْ) [ayah 67]: this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] Subḥān [al-Isrāʾ].

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْنَا يَا نَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ (٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَرْدًا): i.e. "possessed of coolness".
And (عَلَى): attached to سلامًا, or it is an adjective of it.

ukberi-tibyan:72-73.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا صَالِحِينَ (٧٢) وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ الْخَيْرَاتِ وَإِقَامَ الصَّلَاةِ وَإِيتَاءَ الزَّكَاةِ وَكَانُوا لَنَا عَابِدِينَ (٧٣))
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَافِلَةً): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from يعقوب.
It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like العاقبة and العافية, governed by the meaning of «وَهَبْنَا».
And (كُلًّا): the first object of «جَعَلْنَا».
(وَإِقَامَ الصَّلَاةِ): its origin is إِقَامَة, [the tāʾ] being compensation for the omission of one of the two alifs; and He made the muḍāf ilayhi a replacement for the hāʾ [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa].

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلُوطًا آتَيْنَاهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ تَعْمَلُ الْخَبَائِثَ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَاسِقِينَ (٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلُوطًا): i.e. "and We gave Lūṭ".
And (آتَيْنَاهُ): explains the omitted [verb]; likewise: «وَنُوحًا», «وَدَاوُدَ», «وَسُلَيْمَانَ», «وَأَيُّوبَ» and the names of the prophets, upon them be peace, that come after it.
It may also be that the implied form is: "and remember Lūṭ", the implied form being: "and remember the story of Lūṭ"; and the omitted story is what governs «إِذْ». And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:77-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَنَصَرْنَاهُ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ (٧٧) وَدَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِي الْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنَصَرْنَاهُ): i.e. "We protected him from their harm".
It is also said: «مِنْ» is in the sense of على ("against").
And (إِذْ نَفَشَتْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for يحكمان.
And (لِحُكْمِهِمْ): meaning those who disputed over the tillage. It is also said: the pronoun is for them, and for Dāwūd and Sulaymān. It is also said: it is for Dāwūd and Sulaymān specifically, and it is plural because two are a plural.

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ وَكُلًّا آتَيْنَا حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُدَ الْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَالطَّيْرَ وَكُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ (٧٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَعَ دَاوُدَ الْجِبَالَ): what governs «مَعَ» is «يُسَبِّحْنَ», and it is parallel to His saying, Exalted is He: (يَاجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ).
And يسبّحن is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الجبال.
(وَالطَّيْرَ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الجبال. It is also said: it [the wāw] is in the sense of مع ("with", mafʿūl maʿahu).
It is read anomalously in the nominative [وَالطَّيْرُ], conjoined to the pronoun in «يُسَبِّحْنَ».
It is also said: the implied form is: "and the birds likewise".

ukberi-tibyan:80-81.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ مِنْ بَأْسِكُمْ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ شَاكِرُونَ (٨٠) وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ الرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةً تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَالِمِينَ (٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَكُمْ): it may be an adjective of لبوس, or be attached to علّمنا, or to صنعة.
(لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ): it may be a badal (substitute) from لكم with repetition of the preposition; and it may be attached to علّمنا, i.e. "for the sake of fortifying you".
And يُحْصِنَكُمْ with yāʾ, on the basis that the agent is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or Dāwūd, upon him be peace, or the making, or the teaching, or the garment; and with tāʾ, i.e. the craft, or the coats of mail; and with nūn, for Allah the Exalted, by way of majesty.
It is also read with the shadda and light.
And (الرِّيحَ): accusative on the implied form: "and We subjected to Sulaymān"; the first «سَخَّرْنَا» indicates it.
It is also read in the nominative, as a new beginning (istiʾnāf).
And (عَاصِفَةً): a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «تَجْرِي» another ḥāl: either a badal from عاصفة, or [a ḥāl] from the pronoun in it.

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمِنَ الشَّيَاطِينِ مَنْ يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا دُونَ ذَلِكَ وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَافِظِينَ (٨٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to الرياح ("the winds"), or nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf). It is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, and the pronoun refers back to its meaning.
And (دُونَ ذَلِكَ): an adjective of عملًا.

ukberi-tibyan:84-87.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِ مِنْ ضُرٍّ وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنَا وَذِكْرَى لِلْعَابِدِينَ (٨٤) وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ (٨٥) وَأَدْخَلْنَاهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِنَا إِنَّهُمْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (٨٦) وَذَا النُّونِ إِذْ ذَهَبَ مُغَاضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ نَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَى فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ (٨٧))
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَحْمَةً) and (ذِكْرَى): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); it may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [mafʿūl muṭlaq], i.e. "and We had mercy on him".
And (مُغَاضِبًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial).
